articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Complete RFID System in the UHF Band Focused on the Backscattering Communication and Reader Architecture
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: A complete long range passive RFID system, compliant with the EPCGlobal UHF Class 1 Generation 2 standard, and focused on the backscattering tag-to-reader communication, is presented in this paper. Special emphasis has been placed on the reader, whose architecture is entirely designed and analyzed. Effects that degrade reader performance are studied. As a result, guidelines for a proper long range RFID reader design, with the main objective of maximizing the operating distance, are derived.

articleTitle: RFID in Metallic Environment
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: At the Fraunhofer-Institut für Integrierte Schaltungen RFID applications mainly operate in the vicinity of metal. We started to focus on the development of tags for the metallic environment. Actual projects are a Fraunhofer intern project Inguss, which deals with the implementation of sensor tags inside die-cast components. A UHF tag was designed for prototyping reasons and ensuring the feasibility of their usage on metal in a logistics application.

articleTitle: Optimal Impedance Matching in Passive UHF RFID Sensors
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: This paper proposes a method for optimal impedance matching in passive UHF RFID Sensors. The voltage multiplier (VM) is a key subsystem in power recovery circuits. Both its impedance and operation range are optimized. The proposed method evaluates each VM under the same load conditions, thus it can be also used as a comparison tool for different VM structures.

articleTitle: Mobile Multi-Purpose RFID System
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: RFID systems are an important technology that are used for various applications as logistic processes or access control. Today's systems are typically designed for a specific application and deployed by a single party. To identify security requirements for future RFID systems, an aircraft-airport scenario making quite radical assumptions is described. The RFID reading and processing systems are distributed between the airplane, the airport, and various backend processing systems. With RFID readers and processing systems being on-board of aircraft and being dynamically connected to different ground systems, the systems spans multiple administrative domains with dynamically changing topology. The communication is set up spontaneously using both wired and wireless communication. The reference architecture is described, and needed security building blocks are presented that are expected to be useful in such future RFID applications.

articleTitle: Design Methodology of a Voltage Multiplier for Full Passive Long Range UHF RFID
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: The main challenge in a full passive long range RFID tag is operating at high reading distances. The current work shows the main constraints that a RFID system presents. Two of these constraints depend on the Voltage Multiplier. So its critical design makes the Voltage Multiplier methodology presented in this paper very attractive in order to obtain the maximum communication range.

articleTitle: Modelling of HF and UHF RFID Technology for System and Circuit Level Simulations
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: RFID transponders are currently being introduced in many application domains. Actual HF and UHF transponders are generally designed in compliance with existing ISO/IEC standards. Besides the design of RFID transponder chips, packages and appropriate reader front-ends, the wireless transmission link and communication interferences have a strong impact on the overall system reliability. In order to allow directed improvement of RFID systems, integrated models of the electronic parts, the RF front-ends and the wireless communication links are required. In this contribution we present integrated approaches for modelling HF and UHF transponders on different levels of granularity. Based on the complete model of an UHF transponder/interrogator system we will show some simulation results with respect to the overall communication reliability of an RFID system.

articleTitle: Predicting the influence of permittive materials on passive inductive coupled RFID-transponders
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: Today inductive coupled RFID-systems are widely used, e.g. for access control, item tagging or wireless safety systems. The design and optimization of antennas for inductive coupled RFID-transponders require the determination of their electrical properties. This includes the calculation of the inductance and resistance of the antenna coil as well as the prediction of the parasitic capacitance. The parasitic capacitance is given not only by the geometry and material parameters of the antenna coil and substrate material. It is also influenced by environmental conditions. A recent method to predict electrical properties of planar antennas and the transponder respectively was developed in "Cichos, Verfahren zur Modellierung von planaren Spulen für den Entwurf und die Optimierung von Antennenspulen induktiv gekoppelter RFID-Transponder". Based on this method the influence of permittive material in the environment of a RFID-transponder, e.g. lamination foils, paper, water etc. can be calculated. It has been illustrated how these effects can be considered in the development process and technology selection of antenna coils. This paper is based on unpublished results of "Cichos, Verfahren zur Modellierung von planaren Spulen für den Entwurf und die Optimierung von Antennenspulen induktiv gekoppelter RFID-Transponder" during the research work at the Forschungsschwerpunkt Technologien der Mikroperipherik of the Technische Universität Berlin.

articleTitle: New properties of UHF RFID transponders on metal with microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: RFID technology based on UHF frequency has become the most economical identification method, when pallet- size items are being identified full-automatically, with no active human assistance. When goods are travelling long distances, "smart labels" used in disposable packaging are a good choice. In Europe the amount of returnable transport items (RTI) used in supply chain is significant. Typically the RTI's like containers, trolleys and dolly's are metallic. Even non-metallic RTI's like pallets, boxes and crates often contain metallic objects leading to a need of an RFID transponder that works well on metallic objects.

articleTitle: Data Security in RFID on Item Level
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: Applications based on RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) tagging at item level experience a growing diffusion in industrial and retail processes, whereby data security gains on impact. In this context, FIR accomplished a study about "Data Security at Item-Tagging in Apparel Retail" and developed a package of measures. The research work concerning this matter is based on a hybrid approach, whereby the theoretical risk potential in RFID on item level and the necessity of data security was analyzed "top-down" first. On this basis, an empirical study in the apparel retail was accomplished "bottom-up" afterwards, to elicit the key challenges of data security. The cognitions won in this way outline the basis for the development of a package of measures, which eliminates the worked out key challenges of data security in RFID-Item-Tagging.

articleTitle: RFID Usage in Retail beyond the Point of Sale - Temporary Deactivation as a Solution for Challenges in Privacy and Security
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: For a couple of years, major retailers across the world have been integrating RFID applications in their supply chain. The anticipated benefits of RFID usage in retail, however, range much further - beyond the point of sale and into the customer's home. Frequently-cited visions picture fully-automated homes where the microwave oven picks the correct power level by itself and the washing machine autonomously detects the program best suited for the laundry it contains. So far, there are no deployments on a grand scale of RFID technologies beyond the point of sale, primarily due to the cost of transponders. As long as a single RFID tag costs 5¢ and more, attaching one to each item in a retail store does not pay off. Improved production processes and the general trend of decreasing prices for integrated circuits might soon render such scenarios economically feasible, though.

articleTitle: Implementing high-level Counterfeit Security using RFID and PKI
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) systems have become popular mostly for automated identification and supply chain applications. To implement counterfeit security, RFID- and Public Key (PK) technology are combined. RFID tags authenticate themselves by responding to a challenge of a reader/writer device. For this an asymmetric encryption algorithm (RSA) is implemented and executed on the tag. Thereby a high level of counterfeit security is reached. Using a private/public key pair makes this method very flexible for validation by the distributor or the customer. The asymmetric encryption algorithm is running on a low cost tag providing security even for products with a low value. For high level security, drugs are used as example products.

articleTitle: "Smart Logistics" - Usage of innovative Information and Communication technologies in production logistics
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: Innovative data collection technologies such as RFID have proved their practicability and economic efficiency in the fields of trade and stock-keeping, but for the use in the manufacturing industry, however, a number of further uncertainties have to be taken into account. Within the framework of the Sm@rt Logistics project both factors shall be proved in the field of production logistics of a metal-working company. The project and main concepts will be introduced in the article.

articleTitle: SMMART - System for Mobile Maintenance Accessible in Real Time
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: The SMMART integrated R&D project was launched in November 2005 and is planned to run for 3 years. With an overall budget of around 25 millions €, SMMART is partly cofunded by the European Commission under the FP6 joint IST (Information Society Technologies) and NMP (Nanotechnologies and nanosciences, knowledge-based multifunctional materials and new production processes and devices) priority. Coordinated by Turbomeca, the project involves a consortium of 24 partners, well balanced between large industry leaders, small and medium enterprises and research centres from across Europe.

articleTitle: Planning and Analysis of UHF RFID Systems for Consumer Goods Logistics Using Ray Tracing Predictions
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: Tracking of goods within logistics has become an increased area of interest recently. RFID technology in the UHF band is a rather new instrument of tracking goods in this sector. Instead of performing extensive field tests and case studies, this article suggests a simpler and more efficient method of planning UHF RFID systems by using RF propagation results from ray tracing predictions. Two showcase environments, i.e. a receiving area of consumer goods and a warehouse, are presented to be modelled with respect to relevant and realistic occurrences and properties. The ray tracing prediction results allow to analyze and evaluate wave propagation between RFID readers and transponders. From there, system functionality can be deduced.

articleTitle: NFC is the double-click in the internet of the things
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: Evolving from a combination of contactless identification and networking technologies, Near Field Communication (NFC) is a wireless connectivity technology that enables convenient short-range communication between electronic devices. NFC offers the ultimate in convenience for connecting all types of consumer devices and enables rapid and easy communications. It is the perfect solution for controlling data in our increasingly complex and connected world. NFC is central to NXP' vision of a world where everyone can always connect to information, entertainment and services. With NFC, people can come closer and go further. Its intuitive operation makes it particularly easy for consumers to use, while its built-in security makes it ideal for payment and financial applications. Though wireless in nature, NFC is very different from RFID. NFC is a 'usability technology' for consumer devices, adding an easy-to-use wireless interface to deliver connectivity, content and services, while RFID is a technology to improve supply chain and asset management.

articleTitle: Developments in Sensorised Smart RFID Tags Monitoring and Traceability of Sensitive Products
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: This paper summarizes the design and implementation of a new wireless smart sensor which works as a data capturing system with and identifying component. This sensor uses RFID technology in order to meet operation specifications. It has been specially designed to assure the traceability of products which require specific transportation and storage conditions and those which require continuous properties monitoring. Apart from the sensor, the development of a reader with a data treatment and manipulation computer is also offered.

articleTitle: Position Localization for Object Management with the Aid of Passive RFID tags
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: In this paper, a radio frequency localisation system for HF System and UHF System is described. The HF System consists of a HF-Reader, at least four receiving antennas with receive and calibrate modules, three phase detectors, a control module and a PC. The UHF system is optional expandable. In this case, the HF antenna is exchanged though the UHF antenna and the UHF receive and calibrate module. The radio frequency control module steers the identification and localisation process. It collects different values for the positioning calculation as example, the automatic gain control values and the values from the phase detector. The different values are bundled and send to a PC which calculates the 3 D position and steers the robot.

articleTitle: Printed Electronics - From Vision to First Products
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: With printed organic circuits a new kind of electronics is born, which has the potential to revolutionize the spread of today's electronic applications. This innovation is basically possible through inexpensive and fast fabrication methods for the realization of electronic products, like printing techniques using soluble organic materials. A major application for printed electronics is the field of radio-frequency identification (RFID). This application would benefit enormously from low priced electronics that is available in high volumes.

articleTitle: RFID - Logistics and Supply Chain Management
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: The increasing cross-linking within the supply chain - permitted only by the development of complex IT systems - puts new requirements on logistic systems. Modern material flow and information technologies have to ensure the continuous real-time supervision and control of the material flow. Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) is an ideal tool to link the material flow with the information flow at a relatively early stage. The article gives an short overview in how far the Fraunhofer-Institute for material flow and logistics deals with the topic of RFID.

articleTitle: Tracking and Tracing in Production Scenarios with passive RFID Transponders
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: The paper will show new ideas of RFID and real time location systems (RTLS) for production scenarios, e.g. aviation industry and automotive industry. To evaluate different systems of tracking, tracing and identification, it is necessary to design new comparable test approaches. While radio frequency based identification has gained wide acceptance in the market the use of RF-technologies for real-time location is still limited to certain branchspecific approaches, such as in hospitals, car yards or container terminals. One reason for this missing dissemination may be seen in the high costs for the infrastructure since traditionally active transponders or ultra-sound systems are used for real-time location, requiring expensive asset tags and an extensive network of base-stations.

articleTitle: Security challenges for RFID key applications
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: RFID technology is an emerging market with a wide spectrum of application domains. The introduction of RFID systems in industrial manufacturing has already been taken up more than ten years ago. Currently RFID tags are appearing in public environments like ticketing applications and retail supply chains. One the one hand mass ap-plications will imply a break-through for RFID technologies, on the other hand new security issues have to be addressed in order to obtain an add-on benefit compared to classical barcode applications. In this contribution we address RFID security issues in general and related to selected application scenarios. At first we introduce basic RFID security requirements. Subsequently application oriented security measures are discussed for three application scenarios: automotive production, retail supply chains and anti-counterfeiting for pharmaceutical products. Finally challenges and perspectives for future improvements of security measures in RFID systems and privacy issues will be outlined.

articleTitle: Data-on-Tag: An Approach to Privacy friendly Usage of RFID Technologies
publicationTitle: 3rd European Workshop on RFID Systems and Technologies
abstract: The proliferation of RFID technology in many application areas has caused serious concerns regarding threats to consumer privacy. To a large extent, this is due to the widespread approach of storing RFID-based data via a global network (Data-on- Network), enabling its linkage and analysis. Based on a description of existing privacy threats and a presentation of the two general storage approaches, we argue that privacy concerns can be narrowed down by exclusively storing data on RFID tags (Data-on-Tag). We support this assumption by presenting advantages for consumers as well as for companies and describe some novel application areas emerging from tag-centric approaches
